title: Partial credit for two-part items
statement: Whether a two-part claim-and-evidence item should give credit for a right first part alone, or only when both parts are right.
example: On a published test, the first part alone earns 1, both parts 2 and a wrong first part 0.
detail: A review of an outside measurement project found that the published test scores two-part items with partial credit, the first part alone earning 1, both 2 and a wrong first part 0, and that the project's own binary scorer biased ability estimates; it recommended partial-credit scoring with per-part keys for the reading project's own standard (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0072-learnings-from-incept-map-proxy-2026-06-25.qmd`). That project later moved to partial credit (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/HOTBUCKET.md`), while a reading app's server scorer and the staged item standard still score a two-part item only when both parts are right (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0024-beyond-alpharead-pr45-all-qti-types.qmd`, `grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/pr-proposals/ti-courseplans-standards/staged/docs/standards/item-quality.md`). No measured comparison of the two rules was found; to settle it, score the same answers both ways and see which better tracks the published test.
against: A later run found: one package records that the reference test's own technical report scores two-part items all-or-nothing, each part right for credit, and treats its own partial credit as a deviation, its partial-credit confirmation coming from a state test's paper answer keys (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/01_PSYCHOMETRIC_DESIGN.md`).

evidence.quote: **EBSR/Composite = PARTIAL CREDIT (0/1/2)** … Their own MLEF scorer is binary → biases ability. Our standard is SILENT on the scoring model. Action: require polytomous Partial-Credit scoring for EBSR/Composite + per-part answer keys; FAIL binary EBSR scoring.
kb-0072's divergences RESOLVED (bank 38→650; EBSR now PCM 0/1/2)
**EBSR** — Part B uses **verbatim** passage sentences as evidence; **both parts** required to score.
Our EBSR partial-credit scoring (PCM 0/1/2) is a disclosed deviation from MAP's dichotomous composite rule.
the pilot scores every EBSR both ways in parallel — PCM 0/1/2 and dichotomous
the mean absolute linking-residual difference between the two scoring rules, computed on EBSR-heavy sessions (≥3 EBSR items), with a bootstrap 95% confidence interval.

- **Criterion:** dichotomous scoring wins if its linking residuals are lower *and* the CI excludes zero; otherwise PCM is retained. The decision is made before RIT output is unlocked, so the shipped RIT transformation is fitted under the winning rule.

- **Selection caveat, flagged for item-fit analysis:** the PCM step Δ=0.5 also affects Fisher information and therefore item *selection*, not just scoring — the item-fit analysis will examine whether EBSR selection behavior differs materially between rules.
NWEA's Technical Report states composite items are scored dichotomously (students must answer each part correctly for credit).
Composite Item (EBSR) partial credit scoring confirmation: Part A only = 1 point, both parts = 2 points.
**2:** accurate answer AND relevant text evidence. **1:** one part only. **0:** incorrect/blank.
Note that this is a deliberate deviation from MAP: NWEA's Technical Report states that composite items are scored dichotomously (students "must answer each part correctly" for credit).
